summary.text: In a July 2025 official statement as OSTP director, Michael Kratsios described America’s AI Action Plan as charting a course to cement U.S. dominance in artificial intelligence. He later promoted the AI Exports Program as a way to unlock global markets and share a trusted, sovereign AI stack with partners and allies. In February 2026 remarks, he argued that focusing AI policy on safety and speculative risks inhibits a competitive ecosystem, and said use-case and sector-specific regulation best allows adoption. He also stated that AI governance must be local and that the United States totally rejects global governance of AI.

He later promoted the AI Exports Program as a way to unlock global markets and share a trusted, sovereign AI stack with partners and allies.

He also stated that AI governance must be local and that the United States totally rejects global governance of AI.

kids_chatbots.why: Statements about protecting children and empowering parents (s12, s83, s85) concern parental controls and general child safety, not a chatbot ban, age verification, or a legal duty on chatbot makers.

deepfakes.why: No statement addresses deepfake penalties, likeness rights, or takedown duties.

election_ads.why: No statement addresses AI in election ads or political content.

labeling.why: No statement addresses watermarking, AI-content labeling, or chatbot disclosure.

dc_ratepayers.why: He endorses data centers bringing or buying their own power and commits to AI leadership without raising Americans' electricity prices, implying protection against shifting power costs to households.

layoff_reporting.why: No statement addresses reporting or notice of AI-caused layoffs.

training_consent.why: General references to respecting intellectual property (s12) and complaints about foreign model distillation (s26, s27, s73) do not address consent or payment for copyrighted training data.

transparency.why: No statement addresses required safety plans, incident reports, or sharing model information with government.

whistleblowers.why: No statement addresses AI whistleblower protections.

liability.why: No statement addresses developer liability for AI harms or Section 230.

nuclear.why: References to civil nuclear energy (s96, s130) do not address human control of nuclear launch.

autonomous_weapons.why: No statement addresses human control of lethal force or limits on autonomous weapons.

intl_agreement.why: He states the U.S. 'totally reject[s] global governance of AI' and warns international dialogue must not drift toward it, explicitly opposing binding international AI governance.

pause.why: Pro-innovation and 'out-innovate' rhetoric (s189, s42) does not explicitly address a pause or slowdown on frontier AI development.

rsi.why: Support for autonomous AI science (s22, s18) does not address limits on recursive self-improvement or automated AI research.

dc_moratorium.why: Supports infrastructure expansion but does not address a data center moratorium.

bias_audits.why: Criticism of 'woke AI' does not specify opposition to discrimination testing or bias-audit requirements.

preemption.why: References to a national framework and the truncated federal-AI statement do not establish support for overriding state laws.

chips.why: Export advocacy concerns partners and allies; discussion of chip tracking does not establish a position on stricter export controls for rivals.

testing_mandate.why: General criticism of safety-focused policy does not establish opposition to mandatory pre-release testing.

misuse.why: The biological-screening excerpt describes a technical safeguard but does not establish support for a screening requirement or other weapons-misuse rule.

licensing.why: Preference for sector-specific regulation does not establish a position on AI licensing or a new federal AI agency.

superintelligence.why: Promotes superintelligence for scientific discovery but does not explicitly reject or support a ban.

statements.text: America’s AI Action Plan charts a decisive course to cement U.S. dominance in artificial intelligence.

attribution.speaker: Michael Kratsios
attribution.role: Director, Office of Science and Technology Policy

statements.text: By fueling this next phase of the AI Exports Program, we will unlock global markets and opportunities for U.S. companies and workers while cementing America’s position as the indispensable engine of secure, cutting-edge AI with our partners and allies.

statements.text: To give the American people confidence in these tools, the Trump Administration seeks to support legislators as they construct a national policy framework that protects children, prevents censorship, respects intellectual property, and safeguards our workers, families, and communities.

statements.text: Prioritizing AI for your people means pursuing a sovereign AI capability for your country now. This begins with the rapid adoption of the best components of the technology stack available, while your national champions work to develop their own.

statements.text: Harnessing cutting-edge AI for science will dramatically increase the productivity of American scientists and researchers. The Genesis Mission will help America’s scientists automate experiment design, accelerate simulations, and generate predictive models that will lead to breakthroughs in energy, manufacturing, drug discovery, and beyond.

attribution.speaker: Michael Kratsios
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: President Trump’s Genesis Mission is mobilizing America’s unmatched scientific infrastructure and AI ingenuity to double the pace of discovery. These 26 challenges are a direct call to action to America’s researchers and innovators to join the Genesis Mission and deliver science and technology breakthroughs that will benefit the American people

attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Meanwhile, the rise of super intelligence now presents a new revolution in the conduct of research across every scientific discipline.

statements.text: Our flagship whole-of-nation effort is The Genesis Mission, America’s super intelligence for science initiative. In July, the White House announced the expansion of the mission from the DOE to a mobilization of more than 15 federal agencies, and committed $5 billion to solving National Science and Technology Challenges.

attribution.speaker: Michael Kratsios
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Super intelligence promises to be the greatest accelerant of scientific progress in human history, if we match its capabilities with an ecosystem adapted to keep up with its speed and scale.

attribution.speaker: Michael Kratsios
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In the age of super intelligence for science, you can’t do frontier science without access to frontier compute. That’s a scarce resource in even shorter supply in an academic or public laboratory, limiting researchers’ ambitions.

attribution.speaker: Michael Kratsios
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: So I’m very proud to announce that Genesis Mission industry partners are committing $2.4 billion in compute, frontier SI for science models, and other tools for researchers.

statements.text: In parallel, the NSF and DOE are launching a $100 million investment in developing the instrumentation needed for autonomous, SI science, and a nationally integrated research system in which anyone can send their experiments to programmable cloud labs.
